title: Doubt belongs
hookLine: doubt belongs to every tradition's saints: Thomas doubted out loud and was still in the room eight days later
tomorrow: on a holy day, a boy whistled in the middle of prayers. then what?

cards: Someone says something huge happened while you were out, and you say: pics, or it didn't happen. Thomas said nearly that. The other disciples told him they'd seen Jesus risen.

Thomas, called Didymus, the twin, had missed it. His answer: "Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe."

teach.h: AFTER EIGHT DAYS, THOMAS WITH THEM.
teach.b: Here's the surprise. John says that after eight days the disciples were inside again, "and Thomas with them." He didn't leave.
He doubted from inside the circle. And Jesus came and offered him exactly what he'd asked for: the hands, the side. Thomas answered, my Lord and my God.
Churches remember him as Saint Thomas the Apostle, with the doubt still attached to his name. He isn't alone.
In Mark, a father pleading for his son cries, "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief."
And at the very end of Matthew, on the mountain, "they worshipped him: but some doubted." Then Jesus sends them all out, the doubters too.

teach.h: DOUBT IS MET, NOT THROWN OUT.
teach.b: That's the teaching inside these scenes: in the Gospels, doubt is met, not thrown out.
For a rule of your own, a doubt doesn't cancel the practice. You can bring it into the room.

how: Christians read the story of Thomas in John 20 and remember him as Saint Thomas the Apostle. Some find room for honest doubt inside their prayer, as the father in Mark 9 did.

o: a rule that anyone who doubts must leave the group
a feeling that disappears once you finally pray right
doubt can live inside a practice, not only outside it

games.q: your friend in a Bible study says she doubts the resurrection and thinks she should stop coming until she's sure. what fits these Gospel scenes?
o: keep coming: Thomas doubted from inside the room, and was met there.
stay away until the doubt passes, then come back.
keep the doubt secret so no one else is shaken.
games.why: Thomas said he wouldn't believe, and eight days later he was still with the disciples when Jesus came.

practice: Say one honest doubt out loud, quietly, in plain words. Don't answer it or argue with it. Then stay where you are for the rest of the sit, the way Thomas stayed in the room.

wordCard.voice: Doubt belongs: doubt can live inside a practice, as it did for Thomas, who doubted and stayed.
